rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: When escaping special characters using a meta-character like backslash or ampersand, the meta-character has to be escaped first to avoid double-escaping, and conversely it has to be unescaped last to avoid double-unescaping.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
rules.description: Matching HTML tags using regular expressions is hard to do right, and can easily lead to security issues.
An array index is compared to be less than or equal to the 'length' property, and then used in an indexing operation that could be out of bounds.
Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.
DOM functions that act like 'eval' and execute strings as code are dangerous and impede program analysis and understanding. Consequently, they should not be used.

If a dollar assertion '$' appears in a regular expression before another term that cannot match the empty string, then this assertion can never match, so the entire regular expression cannot match any string.

rules.cwe_name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
rules.description: Including functionality from an untrusted source may allow an attacker to control the functionality and execute arbitrary code.
Prepending a backslash to an ordinary character in a string does not have any effect, and may make regular expressions constructed from this string behave unexpectedly.
If an object literal has two properties with the same name, the second property overwrites the first one, which makes the code hard to understand and error-prone.
Checking for the "javascript:" URL scheme without also checking for "vbscript:" and "data:" suggests a logic error or even a security vulnerability.
